title: Axiom of infinity
summary: At least one inductive set exists, supplying enough sets to model the natural numbers.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared first-order set theory context is fixed.

content.plain: At least one inductive set exists, supplying enough sets to model the natural numbers.
content.example: Starting with ∅ and repeatedly adjoining x as a member yields the von Neumann finite ordinals inside I.
content.caveat: Infinity asserts existence; it does not by itself select one unique natural-number object.
